record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: For a brane tiling that is inconsistent in the sense relevant to quiver gauge theories, what is the infrared physics and what is the geometry of the moduli space? Conversely, for consistent brane tilings, can one verify that renormalization-group flow in the field theory reaches the correct geometric moduli space?

evidence.quote: Question 22. Given an inconsistent tiling, what is the infra-red physics, and the geometry of the moduli space? On the other hand, for consistent theories, it would be important to check that the renormalization group flow in the field theory takes one to the correct geometry.

artifact.category_tag: brane tilings and quiver gauge theories
artifact.self_contained_problem:
A brane tiling is a bipartite graph embedded on a two-dimensional torus that encodes a four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theory: vertices (colored black/white) correspond to superpotential terms, faces correspond to U(N) gauge groups, and edges correspond to bifundamental chiral matter fields. The tiling is called consistent (e.g. satisfies the properly-ordered / non-degeneracy conditions, equivalently the associated dimer model has an isoradial embedding and the quiver algebra is a 3-Calabi–Yau algebra) when the resulting gauge theory is expected to flow in the infrared to a superconformal field theory whose mesonic moduli space of vacua reproduces a prescribed toric Calabi–Yau threefold singularity (the one read off from the perfect-matching / characteristic-polynomial data of the tiling). A tiling that fails these consistency conditions is called inconsistent.

(a) For an inconsistent brane tiling, determine the infrared physics of the associated quiver gauge theory (e.g. whether it flows to a nontrivial fixed point, confines, breaks supersymmetry, or develops emergent symmetries) and describe the geometry of its mesonic moduli space of vacua.

(b) For a consistent brane tiling with prescribed toric Calabi–Yau threefold X assigned by the standard combinatorial recipe, prove that the renormalization-group flow of the corresponding quiver gauge theory in the infrared yields a moduli space of vacua isomorphic to X (rather than to some other variety).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is one of several open problems posed in a 2021 survey on quiver gauge theories. No general classification of the IR behavior of inconsistent brane tilings, nor a general proof that consistent tilings flow to the prescribed toric Calabi–Yau geometry, appears in the literature; partial results exist (e.g. for specific families like Y^{p,q} or via a-maximization), but the general statement remains open.
